cultural.vision_reason: The picture shows an elaborate ceremonial helmet made from a gourd, covered in cowrie shell bands and glass beads with antelope horns lashed on — a form of headgear/ritual dress documented among West African groups such as the Konkomba, not a weapon. It is not a "weapon" as claimed, but the object type is plausible for the claimed people and region.

physical.title: helmet
physical.summary: Helmet made of gourd, stitched all over in concentric bands of cowrie shells  interspersed with blue and red glass beads.On the top of the helmet the cowrie shells form a cross pattern and two 53cm long horns [antelope ?] are lashed onto the gourd with cotton. One of the horns has broken away from the gourd. The helmet is fringed with 14cm long strings of double cowrie shells and royal blue and pale blue glass beads. At the back of the helmet, attached by cotton, is a 53cm string of cowries arranged in a herringbone design. The gourd is cracked in many places.
